end.summary:
Discussed physical and chemical changes using ice cream, ghee, water, paper, and chapati examples.
Rohan identified that melting ice cream keeps the same substance and changes its state.
Rohan classified melting ghee, freezing water, and changing paper shape as physical changes.
Rohan identified chapati roasting as a chemical change using new colour, smell, and substance as evidence.
Teach-back was not completed; curd-making was introduced but not answered.
end.parentNote: Asha practised identifying physical changes by checking whether the substance stays the same, rather than relying only on reversibility. Rohan used this method for melting ice cream, ghee, freezing water, and changing paper shape, and corrected the initial mix-up that melting ice is chemical (corrected later in the lesson). They also used new colour and smell to classify chapati roasting as chemical. At home, ask Rohan to sort five everyday changes into physical or chemical and explain what evidence they used.
